assessments.rationale: Using an aluminum or metal housing avoids the release of microplastics and nanoplastics during the manufacturing and molding processes (parameter p, page 80). It also reduces the generation of plastic waste in production (parameter r, page 80), aligning with the ambition to minimize microplastic release during manufacturing (page 7).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Distribution and Use Phase. Metal housing increases the product's weight, which conflicts with lightweight design principles (page 80) and increases transport emissions, and can increase raw material and production costs (page 81).

assessments.rationale: Mechanical fasteners avoid the use of chemical adhesives, thereby reducing emissions to air, water, or soil released during the production process (parameter q, page 80) and minimizing the generation of hazardous chemical waste in production (parameter r, page 80). This supports the zero pollution ambition in production (page 3).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Assembly Efficiency and Use Phase. Mechanical assembly can increase assembly time and part count, potentially increasing material footprint (page 80) and manufacturing complexity, which conflicts with lightweight design (page 80).

assessments.rationale: Brushed DC motors have a simpler manufacturing process that requires less energy and fewer resources in production (parameter g, page 33) compared to BLDC motors, which require complex electronic controllers and rare-earth magnets. This significantly lowers the environmental footprint of manufacturing the product (parameter m, page 33, 80) and reduces manufacturing waste (parameter r, page 80).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Use Phase. Brushed motors are less energy-efficient and have a shorter lifespan, which directly conflicts with the energy efficiency first principle (page 3), energy use requirements (page 33), and product durability (page 33).

assessments.rationale: Passive cooling relies on structural design (vents and integrated heat sinks), eliminating the need to manufacture auxiliary active cooling components. This reduces the consumption of energy and resources in production (parameter g, page 33), lowers the environmental footprint of manufacturing (parameter m, page 33, 80), and minimizes waste generated in production (parameter r, page 80).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Use Phase and Reliability. Passive cooling may lead to higher operating temperatures, potentially reducing the motor's durability and reliability (page 33) and limiting functional performance under heavy use (page 80).

assessments.rationale: A monolithic integrated design simplifies the manufacturing process, reducing the consumption of energy, water, and other resources in production (parameter g, page 33). It minimizes the environmental footprint produced by manufacturing (parameter m, page 33, 80) and reduces manufacturing waste (parameter r, page 80) by eliminating complex connectors, internal wiring, and extra structural interfaces.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: End-of-Life and Repairability. This directly conflicts with circularity aspects, such as repairability, ease of maintenance, refurbishment, and recyclability (page 3, 33), as monolithic components are difficult to disassemble and repair.

assessments.rationale: Corded designs eliminate the need to manufacture lithium-ion batteries, which drastically reduces the consumption of resources in production (parameter g, page 33), avoids the high carbon and environmental footprint of battery manufacturing (parameter m, page 33, 80), prevents hazardous waste generation in production (parameter r, page 80), and avoids chemical emissions to air, water, and soil during battery cell production (parameter q, page 80).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Use Phase. Cordless vacuum cleaners offer greater portability and ease of use, so a corded design conflicts with functional performance and conditions for use (page 80).
